title: ENG-9917 fix: run plugin post_compile hooks at most once per app instance
author: FarhanAliRaza
awaiting: author response to masenf design concern

unresolved.first_comment: P2: Track completed post_compile hooks individually. Because the latch is only set after the whole plugin loop succeeds, a retry after a later plugin raises will start from the first plugin again ... duplicates the earlier mutation

P1: Cached plugins stay skipped. After the first successful app() call, this gate returns the cached ASGI app and never enters _assemble_asgi_app() again. If get_config().plugins is changed on the same App instance ... the new plugin is never inspected

outstanding_asks.ask: Questions the design: recompiling on the same instance without re-running post_compile hooks means newly added pages miss plugin effects; asks whether a legit use case hits this or only tests; suggests running hooks whenever _compile runs, or resetting app state (pages/routes/middleware/lifespan) to make re-__call__ safe
outstanding_asks.evidence: Head commit f315ecf (pushed 2026-07-23T20:16, ~1h40m after the review) only fixes unhashable-plugin tracking and adds a news fragment; no reply from author to masenf

recent_comments.excerpt: It's potentially problematic that we allow a recompile on the same instance, but don't re-run the hooks ... Is there a legit use case where this hits? or does it just happen in testing?
Confidence Score: 5/5. This looks safe to merge.
